clue.text: Require left-winger to return after organised resistance starts

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the heads of the two words are kept
something that returns goes back the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: the opening letter of each word
a red is a socialist or communist, someone on the political left

explanation.surface: A demand that a leftist come back once some organised opposition gets under way.
explanation.walkthrough: A red is crossword shorthand for a communist or socialist, hence any left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: To order something is to demand or require it, as in ordering silence; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Out-of-date food I lend has gone rotten

indicators.note: rotten food has broken down and spoiled, so the letters are broken up and reformed

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Stale food that someone loaned out has spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has gone rotten' reads naturally with the food, but here it is the instruction to rearrange 'food I lend has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something old-fashioned belongs to an earlier period and is no longer current, which is what out-of-date means.

clue.text: Spoil girl's appearance

blocks.note: Di is a girl's name; with the 's it becomes DI'S
a figure is a person's shape or look

explanation.surface: Something ruins how a young woman looks.
explanation.walkthrough: Crosswords often use 'girl' for a short female name such as Di, Ena or Una.
explanation.definitionFit: To disfigure is to spoil or mar the look of something, so the verbs match as synonyms.

clue.text: Develop some Maori penfriends

indicators.note: some of the following words means just a part of their run of letters is wanted

blocks.note: found across the join: maoRI PENfriends

explanation.surface: A few pen pals from New Zealand's Maori people are maturing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that ripens develops to maturity, so the verbs are synonyms in the sense of maturing.

clue.text: Anonymous appearance by the French secret police

blocks.note: a face is the look someone presents
le is French for 'the' before a masculine noun
the SS was the Nazi police and security force

explanation.surface: Undercover French police officers appear without their identities known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' is a regular crossword device for a French article: LE, LA or LES.
explanation.definitionFit: A faceless official is nameless and unidentifiable, which is the sense of anonymous.

clue.text: Disguise cross put up at the main entrance

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up raises it so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: a front is a false appearance put on to hide something
a rood is a crucifix, especially one in a church

explanation.surface: A cross has been disguised and hung up by the building's entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disguise' looks like a verb acting on the cross, but it is a noun for a false front.
explanation.definitionFit: The front door is the principal way into a house, which is what main entrance describes.

clue.text: Hypocrisy about social worker

blocks.note: c is short for circa, Latin for about
ants live in colonies and are the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Accusing a social worker of being two-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' suggests a welfare professional, but the ant is a social insect that works.
explanation.definitionFit: Cant is insincere, pious talk, so it names the hypocrisy of saying what one does not mean.

clue.text: Strongly criticised meat roasted without radicchio trimmings

indicators.note: trimmings are what is cut from the edges, so the outside letters are taken
without means lacking, so the following letters are taken out

blocks.note: lamb is the meat of a young sheep
taken as written
the first and last letters of the salad leaf

explanation.surface: A recipe line: meat roasted, leaving off the bits of radicchio garnish.
explanation.walkthrough: Radicchio is a bitter red salad leaf; only its end letters matter here.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambast someone is to attack them fiercely in words, so lambasted means harshly criticised.

clue.text: Immoral act supported by the church from that time on

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part sits underneath, so it follows the first part

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong or immoral deed
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A wicked deed that the church has backed ever since.
explanation.definitionFit: Since as an adverb means from then until now, the same stretch of time as from that time on.

clue.text: Police officer's position causes frustration

blocks.note: DI is a Detective Inspector; with the 's it becomes DI'S
an appointment is a job or post

explanation.surface: A policeman's new posting leaves him feeling thwarted.
explanation.definitionFit: Disappointment is the feeling when hopes are unmet, close in meaning to frustration.

clue.text: Lack of attention in vehicle leading to senseless crash

indicators.note: in a crash things are smashed and thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: a car is a road vehicle
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A driver not paying attention causes a pointless car accident.
explanation.walkthrough: CAR comes first because it is 'leading'; the crash is the shake-up of 'senseless'.
explanation.definitionFit: Carelessness is a failure to take due care or heed, which is a lack of attention.

clue.text: Antagonise by spreading a neat lie

indicators.note: spreading something moves it about and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Telling a tidy falsehood around is a way to make enemies.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to turn them hostile or unfriendly, which is to antagonise them.

clue.text: PM's not working with a film producer

indicators.note: not here means without, so the following word's letters are left out

blocks.note: David Cameron was the UK Prime Minister when the puzzle appeared; the 's stands for 'is'
a machine that is on is working
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister is idle, along with a movie maker.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop ON from CAMERON and add A for CAMERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A camera produces film images, so it is a playful description rather than a movie studio or producer.

clue.text: Family provided accommodation for taking in harmless old ladies, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the words before it
taking in means letting something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to house someone is to give them somewhere to live
the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A family gave lodging to some harmless elderly women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided accommodation' must be read as one past-tense verb, not as a noun phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A household is everyone living together in one home, which is often a family.

clue.text: Unhappy at EEC roll of voters

indicators.note: something unhappy is out of sorts, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Displeasure at the European Economic Community's register of voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' is part of the fodder, and also suggests the electoral roll. The EEC was the forerunner of the European Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Electoral is the adjective meaning relating to elections or the electorate, the body of people who vote.

clue.text: I notice Sid turning up with Ned to be sneered at

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning something up flips it so it reads from the bottom

blocks.note: taken as written
an ad is a notice advertising something
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone spots Sid arriving with Ned, both of whom are scorned.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of 'I notice Sid' is reversed, giving DIS DA I, then NED follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To disdain someone is to treat them with contempt, so disdained means scorned or sneered at.

clue.text: Could be a test of judgement

indicators.note: could be suggests a possible alternative form, so the letters may become something else

blocks.note: the five letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Something might be a trial of someone's discernment.
explanation.definitionFit: Good taste is the ability to judge what is fine or fitting, a sense of judgement in aesthetic matters.

clue.text: Ending of hangings in small Eastern country causes a thrill

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so just that one is kept
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
E is the abbreviation for East
the final letter of the word
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Executions in a small Eastern state create a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: S and E come first; the final S of 'hangings' goes inside NATION after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: A sensation is a burst of excitement or a feeling of thrill, so a thrill is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Abnormally large award gets extremely sensitive

indicators.note: extremely here means at the extremes, so only the two end letters are kept

blocks.note: the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone receiving a medal is very touchy about their size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely sensitive' reads as 'very touchy', but it means the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese describes a body much heavier than normal, so abnormally large fits as a description.

clue.text: Home team appears during second half of conference

indicators.note: the second half of a word is its back five of ten letters, so the front is discarded
appearing during something is happening in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a side is a sports team
the back half of the ten-letter word

explanation.surface: The home team turns up in the latter part of a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home team' reads as one sporting phrase, but the clue splits it: Home is the definition and team the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is the place where someone lives, so it is a formal synonym of home.

clue.text: Being included in document I type

indicators.note: included in means contained inside the words that follow, as a run of letters

blocks.note: found across the words: documENT I TYpe

explanation.surface: Someone is mentioned within a document that the speaker is typing.
explanation.definitionFit: An entity is a thing with its own existence, and a being is likewise anything that exists.

clue.text: Subject of article by setter

blocks.note: the is the definite article
the setter writing the clue refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The topic of a piece written by the crossword's compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic or main idea of a piece, so subject is a direct synonym.

clue.text: At the outset, runner has trouble with techniques for tracks

indicators.note: the outset of a word is its beginning, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
to ail is to be troubled or unwell
ways are methods of doing things

explanation.surface: An athlete struggles early on with methods for running on the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' and 'tracks' paint athletics; tracks are in fact rail lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Railways are the lines of rails trains run on, so tracks is a fair synonym in the plural.

clue.text: Lots of young men hide love

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it inside, out of sight

blocks.note: lads are boys or young men
love is zero in tennis scores, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Plenty of young men keep their romances secret.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside LADS, between LA and DS.
explanation.definitionFit: Loads is informal for a great quantity, used just as lots is.

clue.text: Ruler is found in and about Sarajevo

indicators.note: found in means located within the following words as a run of letters

blocks.note: found across the words: abouT SARajevo

explanation.surface: A monarch is seen in and around the Bosnian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in and about' reads like 'in and around' Sarajevo; 'about' is in fact where the letters start.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia, so he is a type of ruler.

clue.text: Typical politician

blocks.note: first meaning: characteristic of a class, a fair sample
second meaning: a person elected to act for others in a legislature

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sneer at an ordinary politician; the two words are separate senses, adjective and noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A representative sample is typical, and an elected member who acts for constituents is their representative.

clue.text: Announced race led surprisingly by Democrat

indicators.note: something that turns out surprisingly is not as expected, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics
the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: News that a Democrat unexpectedly headed an election contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'led' does double duty in the surface; it belongs to the fodder, while 'by Democrat' puts D in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare is to state publicly, so declared is a synonym of announced.

clue.text: Forwards son's aims

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
ends are goals or purposes

explanation.surface: The goals of a boy who passes things on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forwards' looks like a plural noun, as in football, but it is the verb meaning passes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter is to send it on, so forwards and sends are verb synonyms.
